To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presented analytical calculation method is able to predict the flow behavior inside the printing needle with sufficient precision, (ii) the presented approach with the dimensionless flow parameter is a powerful tool for process design in bioprinting, (iii) the presented approach is transferable to different bioinks and (iv) cells influence the printing process in terms of shear stress, aggregation and viability.

the printing process can be described by an analytical model, that this model allows the prediction of shear parameters and that the shear parameters are relevant for the viability of the printed cells.
the presented calculation method allows the estimation of pressure drop and maximum shear stress at the outlet of the printing needle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of extrusion based biomanufacturing of complex 3D structures with regard to shape fidelity and cell viability.
an understanding of the complex interactions of bioink, cells and mechanical forces in the bioprinting needle.
the development of an efficient and reproducible extrusion based biomanufacturing process, which can be applied for the generation of complex 3D tissue constructs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a systematic analysis of the extruded bioink in the printing needle, based on a Hershel Bulkley model is necessary for process optimization concerning processing time, shape fidelity of 3D constructs and cell viability.
the cell size is the most important parameter for the process.
cell viability is strongly dependent on cell size and shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented analytical calculation method is able to predict the flow behavior of the bioinks and the shear forces inside the printing head.
a combination of analytical and numerical modelling enables the user to design a bioprinting setup with regard to cell viability and shape fidelity.
the presented analytical calculation method can be used to describe the flow in the printing head and to estimate the shear parameters in the outlet.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of analytical and numerical modelling can provide valuable insight into the extrusion based 3D biomanufacturing process, and that the proposed approach allows the user to optimize the process parameters with regard to the rheological properties of the bioink, cell viability, printing speed, shape fidelity and the dimension of the printed strands.
the printing needle diameter is the most important parameter for the process design, followed by the printing pressure and the rheological behavior of the bioink.
it is possible to predict the flow behavior of a bioink and to optimize the process parameters to achieve a certain flow behavior.
